title: Systemic and Mucosal HIV-1 gp120-Reactive Responses After Oral Hyperimmune IgY in Outbred Cats
content: Antibody-network mechanisms require evidence beyond antigen binding. We reconciled surviving records from two independent feline experiments involving oral hyperimmune anti-HIV-1 gp120 immunoglobulin Y (IgY). Cohort A comprised six adult cats receiving hyperimmune or matched non-hyperimmune IgY (three per group); Cohort B comprised 42 different cats receiving hyperimmune egg-yolk preparation (n = 18) or matched control (n = 24). Supplied serum OD450 values were 0.329, 0.544 and 0.775 versus 0.093, 0.106 and 0.122; two exposed values exceeded the historical 0.35 boundary. Reported competitive inhibition was 11.1–15.8% versus 1.3–2.0%. A reconstruction preserved the published dilution-dependent JR-FL profile, but disagreement between graphical and numerical records prevented verification of neutralisation titres. Salivary anti-gp120 IgA was classified positive in 18/18 exposed cats; controls comprised 20 negative and four borderline animals, with none classified positive. The categorical comparison gave a nominal Fisher exact P < 0.0001, assuming independent cats. Reagent descriptions, historical assay calibration and allocation records remain incomplete. Oral hyperimmune IgY exposure was associated with recorded gp120 reactivity and salivary IgA responses. These exploratory observations do not establish an Ab1–Ab2–Ab3 cascade, broadly neutralising antibodies or protective efficacy.
